newsitem.title: USA: U.S. blue chip stocks broadly weaker at midday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. blue chip stocks broadly weaker at midday.

text.p: U.S. blue chip stocks were broadly weaker by midday on Monday, as the stock market took a pause after its recent surges higher.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average, which ended at record highs Friday, was down around 55 points at 7742. The late-morning slide prompted the New York Stock Exchange to set curbs on index arbitrage trading.
But the Nasdaq composite was up 1.18 points at 1448.28
"The market is catching its breadth," Ken Ducey, vice president and director of trading at BT Brokerage, said.
Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd, said: "It's a low conviction sell-off. There's a smattering of profit-taking, while other issues are continuing their rally."
Among Dow component stocks, Philip Morris Cos Inc shares were under pressure dipping one to 44-5/8 after news of proposed $368.5 billion settlement between the tobacco industry.

The tobacco accord, announced late Friday afternoon, would require tobacco companies to pay $368.5 billion over 25 years to compensate states and smokers for medical treatment and other smoking-related costs.
RJR Nabisco Holdings Inc stock was up 3/8 at 34-7/8.
The Dow's weakness was also partly attributed to Friday's triple-witching expiration of index futures and options.
"Stocks are a little on the soft side after triple-witching on Friday, but that's normal," Dick Stein, vice president of U.S. Clearing Corp, said.
Sell programs contributed to the market's softer tone at the open, said Gregory Nie, technical analyst at EVEREN Securities Inc.
Takeover announcements created most activity in the stock market, particularly among computer systems companies, analysts said.
Shares of Tandem Computers Inc surged 6-1/4 to 21-1/4 after personal computer supplier Compaq Computer Corp said it agreed to acquire Tandem in a stock swap valued at about $3 billion.
Compaq stock was down 1-3/4 at 105-1/8.
In the energy sector, Pennzoil Co stock roared 18-5/8 points higher to trade at 78-1/4.

Union Pacific Resources Group Inc said it renewed its attempts to acquire Pennzoil after its previous advances were rebuffed, offering a two-step cash and stock transaction valued at about $6.4 billion.
Union Pacific Resources stock was off 5/8 at 25-3/4.
Among bank shares, Dime Bancorp Inc said it had a definitive agreement to acquire North American Mortgage Co in an all-stock deal valued at about $374 million.
Dime's stock was down 7/8 at 18-1/8 while North American Mortgage was up 1-1/8 at 24-1/4.
((Wall Street desk 212-859-1730))
